top_choice_rationale: P002 honours a clean, universal mechanism: Halperin-Nelson (1978) and Young (1979) predicted the hexatic phase and defect-unbinding melting in two dimensions, with testable exponents later checked in colloids, liquid-crystal films and hard-disk simulations, and the three originators exactly fill the three-person limit. The citation is narrow (theory of two-dimensional melting and the hexatic phase) so it stays distinct from the 2016 Kosterlitz-Thouless prize, and the remaining dispute over the order of the liquid-hexatic step is anticipated by the theory itself. P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) is a mature, independently confirmed and well-allocated second choice, but it is a precision refinement of a line honoured in 2005 and 2012 and its priority record is unsettled, so I rank it below the conceptual advance; any award is better than none.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I am the proposer of B020 and the only soft-matter/statistical-physics voice, but have no known collaboration with Halperin, Nelson or Young, nor with Katori or Ye
